essential_indicators.text:
Health and safety management system:
a.  Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the
    entity? (Yes/ No). If yes, the coverage such system?
     Yes, ISO 45001:2018 Occupational Health and Safety Standard is being adopted at the Bank. During FY2026, eleven
   new locations were added, taking the total to 32 premises like large offices, call centres, data centres, learning centre
    and staff quarters.

b. What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and
    non-routine basis by the entity?
    The Bank has a process for identifying work related hazards, including collecting and reviewing all available
     information about potential and actual problems and periodic inspection of the workplace. A systematic approach
    has been adopted which involves division of the workplace into major areas like workstation, utility, storage,
     processing, customer service, and others, and with appropriate measures identified for the respective locations. The
    Bank has established a robust process for dealing with electrical and fire hazards including regular testing, ensuring
    use of protective equipment and training for emergency preparedness. Also, effective work permit system is in place
     to improve operational efficiency, enhance safety and security exposure and reduce risk of accidents within the
    Bank's premises.

    At the Bank's large offices, key activities include maintaining inventory of materials and material safety data sheets,
     periodic testing for air, noise and illumination quality, an online system for recording safety related complaints from
    employees, and logs of maintenance. Further, there is ongoing evaluation of business centres and other premises for
     structural damages, and its relocation if required. Dedicated persons have been appointed for oversight on all work-
     related issues at the Bank's premises and addressing concerns as well as maintaining reports and data on health
    and safety related matters.

c.  Whether you have processes for workers to report the work-related hazards and to remove

     Yes, the Bank has a process for reporting work related hazards. All large offices have designated managers, zonal

   A tab "Report a Safety Incident" is available on the Bank's intranet to report and address safety related incidents.

    strategy adopted by your company to reduce usage of hazardous and toxic chemicals in your
    products and processes and the practices adopted to manage such wastes.
     ICICI Bank's commitment to sustainability extends to efficient management of all waste generated at its facilities.
    There is a robust process for handling and composting organic waste in large premises. E-waste is handed over for
     recycling to authorised agencies in compliance with various national and local regulations on waste management.
     In FY2026, the Bank enhanced efforts on circularity in waste and water, and expanded measures like sewage waste
    treatment plant and waste water recycling at new premises. The Bank has introduced several measures, including
    proper waste segregation at the site for suitable treatment according to type of waste, to enable waste reduction
    and recycling at its ICICI Service Centre at Bandra-Kurla Complex in Mumbai, Maharashtra. The Bank has also
    advocated the use of environment-friendly consumables with the aim of promoting sustainable processes. The ICICI
     Service Centre is certified as IGBC Platinum, ‘Net Zero Waste to Landfill’, and as per ISO 14001:2015 and ISO
    45001:2018 standards.

leadership_indicators.text:
Does the entity have a business continuity and disaster management plan? Give details in 100
   words/web link.
    The Bank has a defined Business Continuity Management (BCM) (including disaster management) plan to ensure
     continuity of critical services to customers and availability of critical systems during significant disruptions under
     defined disaster scenarios. In the event of a disaster, the Bank endeavours to resume business and operations to an
    acceptable level as per the defined Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) detailed in the plan. The RTO provides guidance
     for prioritizing activities, whenever necessary. There can be external factors beyond the Bank's control, which could
     affect the actual RTO. The BCM plans are reviewed and maintained to incorporate changes in the organization or
    environment and are subject to modification based on the reviews, situations, circumstances, etc. The efficacy of the
   BCM plan is established through periodic business continuity testing. The Bank also has a Disaster Recovery (DR) plan
     to ensure continuity of critical services to customers and availability of identified critical systems in the event of disaster
      (IT system disruption). The DR plans for the identified critical applications are reviewed and maintained to incorporate
    changes in the application or environment and are subject to modification based on the reviews. The efficacy of the DR
    plan is established through periodic DR testing by way of DR drills as per published annual DR calendar.

leadership_indicators.text:
Steps taken to inform and educate consumers about safe and responsible usage of products and/
    or services.
    The Bank aims to treat its customers fairly and provide transparency across its offerings. Continuous customer
    education efforts are made to enable customers to make informed choices regarding banking products and services.
    The Bank also seeks to ensure that the products offered are based on an assessment of the customer’s financial
    needs.
    The Bank regularly conducts customer awareness campaigns through social media, notifications on mobile apps,
    e-mails and SMS, in English and several regional languages, regarding safe banking, cybersecurity as well as

     prevalent modus operandi of frauds. The Bank displays the awareness messages during new payee addition, high
    value fund transfer transactions to create awareness in the transaction flow. In addition to proactively undertaking
    customer awareness campaigns, the Bank creates awareness using other means like,
    •   Safe Banking Tips - detailed 'Do's and Don'ts' are updated on the website www.icici.bank.in

    •   Messages along with statement of accounts, physical and online

    •   Messages printed on Bank's stationery and inserts in deliverables

    •  SMS alerts

    •   Message on phone banking when the customer calls

    •   Posters at branches and ATMs.

    The Bank also displays relevant messages at its offices and business centres for customer awareness. During FY2024
    and FY2025, the Bank conducted an extensive public awareness campaign on fraud prevention on television and
     social media which was well-received. Further, recognizing financial literacy as a need for customers, since FY2021
    the Bank has been publishing The Orange Book, a monthly e-magazine in English that covers an array of financial
     topics from investment planning, safe banking to tax savings, financial preparedness and much more. The Bank
    has made a dedicated #BeatTheCheat campaign to spread awareness on modus operandi and pretext used by
     fraudsters to defraud customers. Awareness, through videos made in 11 regional languages, are related to lottery
     frauds, fake mobile numbers updated in search engines, fraud using QR codes, fake apps and parcel/digital arrest
    scam providing scenarios and fraud prevention tips. The Bank has made fraud awareness videos in Marathi, Hindi
    and English for the Maharashtra police to spread awareness related to social media fraud and know-your-customer
    (KYC) fraud. Fraud awareness pamphlets in 11 regional languages were shared with the Bank’s branches across
     India to be distributed to walk-in customers.

b. What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and

    The Bank has a process for identifying work related hazards, including collecting and reviewing all available
     information about potential and actual problems and periodic inspection of the workplace. A systematic approach
    has been adopted which involves division of the workplace into major areas like workstation, utility, storage,
     processing, customer service, and others, and with appropriate measures identified for the respective locations. The
    Bank has established a robust process for dealing with electrical and fire hazards including regular testing, ensuring
    use of protective equipment and training for emergency preparedness. Also, effective work permit system is in place

    Bank's premises.

     1.   Identifying potential hazards and risks associated with specific activities, processes, or environments through
        Hazard Identification & Risk Assessment (HIRA);

     2.   Evaluating likelihood and potential consequences of these risks;

     3.   Prioritizing risks based on their significance and potential impact on safety, health, and the environment;

     4.   Developing strategies to control, reduce, or eliminate significant risks through engineering controls, administrative
          controls, and/or personal protective equipment (PPE);

     5.   Periodically reviewing and reassessing risks to ensure ongoing effectiveness of risk management measures;

    At the Bank's large offices, key activities include maintaining inventory of materials and material safety data sheets,
     periodic testing for air, noise and illumination quality, an online system for recording safety related complaints from
    employees, and logs of maintenance. Further, there is ongoing evaluation of business centres and other premises for
     structural damages, and its relocation if required. Dedicated persons have been appointed for oversight on all work-
     related issues at the Bank's premises and addressing concerns as well as maintaining reports and data on health
